definition: An antiderivative reverses differentiation. Indefinite integrals represent families of functions and therefore require a constant of integration; initial conditions select one member.

The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects accumulation and instantaneous rate. Differentiating an accumulation function recovers the integrand, while evaluating an antiderivative computes net accumulation.
Substitution reverses the chain rule. A successful substitution matches an inner expression with its derivative factor and transforms limits when working with a definite integral.
